questions.question_text: Why is saving early important for teens?

options.text: It helps buy expensive gadgets immediately.
It gives more time for money to grow and builds financial discipline.
It guarantees a high-paying job in the future.
It prevents the need for a bank account.Correct Answer: B) It gives more time for money to grow and builds financial discipline.
Interest earned only on the initial amount saved.
A fee charged by banks for saving money.
Interest earned on the initial amount and on the interest already earned.
A type of loan for teens.Correct Answer: C) Interest earned on the initial amount and on the interest already earned.

questions.question_text: Which savings option is best for a teen wanting easy access to their money for short-term needs?

options.text: Fixed Deposit (FD)
Recurring Deposit (RD)
Minor Savings Account in a Bank
Long-term Government BondCorrect Answer: C) Minor Savings Account in a Bank

questions.question_text: What is a key benefit of a Post Office Savings Account for teens?

options.text: It offers the highest interest rates compared to banks.
It is government-backed, safe, and accessible in many areas.
It allows unlimited withdrawals without any fees.
It provides a credit card for teens.Correct Answer: B) It is government-backed, safe, and accessible in many areas.

questions.question_text: What is the first step in saving for a big goal like higher education or a vehicle?

options.text: Withdraw money from a savings account.
Define the goal by specifying the amount needed and timeline.
Spend extra money on wants to stay motivated.
Open multiple bank accounts for different goals.Correct Answer: B) Define the goal by specifying the amount needed and timeline.

questions.question_text: How can a teen save for a big goal like a ₹12,000 phone in one year?

options.text: Save the entire amount at once in a Fixed Deposit.
Break it down to save ₹1,000 per month and track progress.
Borrow the money from a friend and repay later.
Ignore smaller expenses to save faster.Correct Answer: B) Break it down to save ₹1,000 per month and track progress.
